- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak for next 7 days.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from 80+), model often lags; adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 day lag in decline.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67); apply +2% bias to forecast mean.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.67 → -0.38 → +0.67), model misreads momentum; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3 days.
